title: Shortest Word Transformation Sequence
statement: You are given two lowercase words begin_word and end_word of equal length, and a list word_list of lowercase words that are all the same length as begin_word. A transformation sequence is a list of words w0, w1, ..., wk where w0 is begin_word, wk is end_word, every adjacent pair differs in exactly one letter position, and every word after w0 (that is, w1 through wk) appears in word_list. Note that begin_word itself does not need to appear in word_list. Return the number of words in the SHORTEST such sequence (its length, counting both begin_word and end_word). If no transformation sequence exists, return 0. If begin_word already equals end_word and end_word is present in word_list, the shortest sequence is the single word begin_word, so return 1.
hints: Each word is a node and two words are connected when they differ in exactly one letter; you need the fewest hops between two nodes in an unweighted graph. Which traversal finds shortest paths?

Run BFS from begin_word. Do not build the whole graph up front: generate a word's neighbors on the fly by trying every letter 'a'-'z' at each position and keeping only results that are in a set built from word_list.

Seed the queue with (begin_word, 1), and mark a word visited the moment you ENQUEUE it, not when you dequeue it, so it never enters the queue twice. When you dequeue end_word, return its stored count directly; because you count words (begin_word is 1) rather than edges, the hit->cog example yields 5, not 4.
